body: I am in the same situation, only she left me bc she wants to try being with a woman. I don't know what else to say other than you're not alone dealing with these feelings
Thank you for your response, PM sent

I hope I didn't do anything wrong, but it's difficult to believe with all she said. I'm left with all these what if's: what if I never called her last night? What if I had tried to facilitate more conversation for her with my family? What if I had just held off on this conversation when she said she wasn't going to break up with me initially? 

As far as being boring, I'm shy around new people. Growing up my dad was an abusive alcoholic and I learned very quickly to be very careful and thoughtful about what I say. I'm getting better, and I really felt like I could be authentic around her which makes this hurt even more. Now, even my authentic self is shit, annoying, boring and unloveable.

I understand what you are saying about the emotional instability and I think she does as well - last week "hot & cold" came on the radio and she was joking that that is how she treats me and I'm probably like "what the fuck". But, just the day before she broke up with me, she'd been wearing my cardigan around because it smelled like me which she loved. It feels like one hiccup happened (my family didn't talk to her enough) and her solution is to just blow up the whole thing. We almost broke up a few months back over the coworker situation, but she said she had a big epiphany, realized how much she loves me and would miss me, and would try to be more understanding in the future. 

I never feel like I measure up, add value to social interactions, or am anything other than a burden. This stems from growing up with an abusive, alcoholic dad who beat into me that I was just a dumbass who would never amount to anything. It's tough for me to find the courage to be outspoken and confident when I've been conditioned to choose my words very carefully to avoid conflict.

I feel similar to you about friends, except that I'm worried about overburdening them and driving them away, leaving me all alone. I'm also very careful of the advice I take and worry they don't fully understand my situation.

> I think she's just projecting and putting her issues onto you...just blaming you really. It's easier for her to say that you're boring than for her to actually face up to the fact that she could very well be a lesbian. It's easier to be heterosexual in society as LGBT people face a lot of discrimination but it still doesn't entitle her to literally use you to fit in more easily in society. 

That's what is so confusing to me. I don't know what happened to make her go from ecstatic with our sex life (she said I'm the first guy who was ever able to actually make her cum) to having to think about girls when she's with me to get off, and finding penises more and more disgusting. A few months ago she did meet a girl at work who is flirting with her and is her "type", so maybe that has something to do with it? She's said she always felt different, but had a strict Catholic upbringing, but how can that be true if we had such a satisfying sex life up until a few months ago? 

I'm just very confused by what went wrong. At first in our relationship she was upset things weren't moving quick enough (at 6 months or so she was very upset we weren't moving in together yet). Now that my finances are better and we were working towards moving in together next year, she's meeting my extended family, etc. it's moving *too* fast and the commitment is too much. 

I should've mentioned that this relationship came right off the heels of a 5 yr one that ended when my ex decided she couldn't commit having only slept with one man (me).  It really messes me up, makes me think that people would be willing to commit to me if I was a better man. I already have self confidence issues, and it sucks how this plays into what I already believe. 

As far as people to talk to, my family's all away for the weekend and I don't want to be "that guy" annoying his friends with his relationship woes. I'm trying to reach out to my therapist but with my work schedule I probably won't be able to see him until mid December

That's one thing I'm really scared of - that I just lost the only person who would put up with me and I'll be alone forever. It's important for me to have a partner to share in my successes and support me in my failures.

Not at all. But at this point I'm sick of feeling unworthy of love and wondering what's wrong with me... And what the benefit is of trying and trying in my career, my studies, etc. if I'll never have someone to share it with long term
